# Agent consumption contract

1. Discover candidate entries from index.json using their descriptions. Read the selected entry's itonami.json for useWhen, avoidWhen, inputs, outputs, effects, authority, sourceRefs and validation. Discovery is not installation or permission.
2. Resolve this registry to one immutable Git commit. Fetch index.json and every file under the selected entry folder from that commit. Compute SHA-256 over sorted relative POSIX paths, each followed by NUL, then the file bytes followed by NUL. Compare sha256:<hex> with the index. Never mix revisions.
3. Inspect catalog provenance. Source file hashes identify the pinned derivation inputs; entry checksums identify the adapted published artifacts. They are different identities. Original profiles are not imported or kept in sync.
4. Resolve local dependencies in this registry. Resolve external references with registry ID, pinned commit, entry ID and that registry's checksum. Unresolved dependencies block use. Plain Hermes consumers do not gain federation support from these documents.
5. Skills: copy the entire selected skill folder into the client's chosen skill directory. Supplemental itonami.json is data for readers that understand it; SKILL.md is the skill entrypoint.
6. Agents: AGENT.md is a reusable role prompt. templates/hermes is a partial scaffold with no identity or enabled tools. Bind target repository parameters, fresh profile identity, owner-reviewed policy, model/provider and effective tool allowlist in the target repository. Never overwrite an existing profile. Choose the target runtime's native configuration and inspect its effective permissions. No automatic materializer is provided.
7. MCP: install the pinned owning runtime separately with its dependencies. Resolve manifest placeholders to the selected absolute checkout path before native client configuration. tools/list is discovery only; authorization is tool-specific. Never infer read-only permission from this entry. Do not invoke fleet calls, sync or provisioning to verify installation unless explicitly authorized.
8. Workflows: workflow.json uses itonami.workflow.v1, an inert recipe schema checked by this repository. Execution requires a reader and target-bound inputs/authority. Hermes manifest compatibility is not executor qualification.
9. tools.json indexes native schemas by provider. Hermes-plugin tools require the pinned plugin and its dependencies; MCP tools require the named MCP connection. A listed capability or tool is neither a runtime grant nor proof of availability.
10. Validate the relevant behavior in the target runtime and store its receipt there. Catalog validation, MCP initialization, tool discovery, simulation, scheduled firing and live hardware qualification are distinct evidence boundaries. This registry enables none of them automatically.

Maintain with scripts/validate.py, scripts/build_index.py and --check. CI performs offline checks; docs/validation.json records the bounded protocol probe. Do not commit credentials, per-bot identities, sessions, cron execution state or ledger contents.

For additional candidates, read catalogs/inventory.json and docs/inventory-2026-10-10.md. Inventory records are source references, not installable entries. Only index.json entries have checked folder artifacts. Recheck the owner contract before use; a filename survey does not qualify runtime or grant authority.

Remaining-candidate decisions are in catalogs/candidate-reviews.json and docs/candidate-review-2026-10-11.md. Only index entries are installable artifacts/scaffolds. The itonami-fleet-catalog native guest host publishes fleet_search only; do not inherit the older JVM adapter toolset. ZAP references require the owner plugin, dependencies, target configuration and caller authorization; registration does not configure or scan targets.

Targeted public-source reviews outside the original two-organization survey are recorded separately in catalogs/targeted-public-sources.json. They preserve the dated survey counts and bind public visibility, reviewed owner revision and exact registry entry provenance. The abaki role retains its canonical profile, Python pipeline and reports in etzhayyim/com-etzhayyim-abaki.

The mihari and dandori MCP entries connect to stdio servers in cloud-itonami/app-itonami-mihari and cloud-itonami/app-itonami-dandori. Their tools are pure functions over the text or issues the caller passes: Sentry data grouping and triage rules, and Linear export conversion, cycle progress, estimate and SLA checks. They do not contact sentry.io or linear.app and store nothing. Registration does not add them to any profile; a profile owner adds an mcp_servers entry, and itonami-agent does not start MCP subprocesses on peer runs.

The kaikei MCP entry connects to a stdio server in cloud-itonami/kaikei. Its tools are pure functions over the journal text or ledger the caller passes. They import MoneyForward, freee, Yayoi, QuickBooks Online and Xero journal exports into a kaikei.ledger.v1 ledger, check it, build a trial balance, P&L or balance sheet (kaikei, QuickBooks Report or Xero Reports shape), and convert between these formats. They also read and write invoices (Xero, QuickBooks Online, freee請求書 and MoneyForward クラウド請求書; Zoho Invoice and FreshBooks read only), compute consumption tax once per invoice per rate, check the contents a Japanese qualified invoice must state, and post invoices as receivable or payable entries (the itonami-invoices skill). They read bank and card statements the user downloaded (OFX/QFX/QBO, 全銀 data, freee, MoneyForward, Xero and QuickBooks statement CSV, bank and card CSV) and Ramp, Brex, Expensify and BILL exports, reconcile statement and ledger balances, suggest invoice settlements, matches, transfers and journals from the user's rules and past journals, and post only the lines the user approved (the itonami-statement-reconciliation skill). A registration number is checked for its form only. They contact no accounting, invoicing, expense or AP service, no bank or card issuer and no NTA site, make no payment, and store nothing. A ledger given to an agent on a remote inference rail leaves the machine through that rail.
